channel.description: The contact's channel the message consumes: the address or the LinkedIn profile it goes to. Exactly that one channel is projected into `contacts[0].channels`.

message.description: What goes out: one format of the channel's, and its text — final, exactly as the person approving it reads it, or a template the provider fills in for the person, on an email, a LinkedIn message or an InMail.

format.description: `email` on the email channel; on LinkedIn, a message to a connection, an InMail, or a voice message the provider speaks from the text.

compose.description: `text`, or absent: the subject and the text are final and go out exactly as written. `template`: both are templates in the template standard the contracts README publishes, which the provider fills in for the person; an email, a LinkedIn message and an InMail may be one, a voice message may not. The bounds below hold a template as written. Its length is the length once the provider fills it in, within the call or later: a text found too long within the call fails `message_too_long`, and one found too long later fails the send then.

subject.description: The subject: one line, something other than white space, at most 998 characters on an email and 200 on an InMail. Only those two formats take one, and both require it.

body.description: The text as plain text, something other than white space — for a voice message the text the provider speaks: at most 12000 characters on an email, the most `conversation.get` reads back of one message; 8000 in a LinkedIn message, 1900 in an InMail and 1000 in a voice message, the most each holds.

send_after.description: The moment the provider sends it at, with its offset, written as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` with a fraction of one to three digits where it names one and `Z` or `+hh:mm` or `-hh:mm`, `T` and `Z` in capitals. Absent, or a moment already past, means as soon as the provider can. Only a plugin whose manifest lists it for the channel takes it, and the claim refuses it on any other (`argument_unsupported`).

follows.description: The earlier letter of this campaign the message follows, as a reply in that letter's thread. Absent: the runtime decides at the claim, and follows the line's root, the latest earlier letter to this person in this campaign on the same channel that itself follows nothing, counted as a touch, holding the provider's reference and not taken back. A work item's identifier: that letter, named explicitly. `new_thread`: a letter of its own. Never null. The default never takes as its root a letter a succeeded `message.status` of the campaign says failed or was cancelled, unless a read of it says it went or may have gone (`sent` or `unknown`). A letter the routed plugin cannot place in a thread goes as a new letter, and the preview a person reads says so; only a letter named explicitly that cannot be followed is refused, at the claim. A letter named explicitly that a read says failed or was cancelled is not refused for that at the claim: it is passed to the provider, which refuses it at its moment where it holds that the letter never went, and nothing is sent. A work item's identifier is taken only by a plugin whose manifest lists `follows` for the channel, and the claim refuses it on any other (`argument_unsupported`), while `new_thread` asks nothing of the plugin and is taken by every one. The runtime's decision is the root `follows`; the arguments stay as the caller wrote them.

sender.description: The provider's account the message goes from, as `sender.list` listed it on the channel the message consumes: its identifier, and its address — null only for an account the provider holds no address for — so the person approving the message reads whose account it goes from.

channels.description: Only the channel the message consumes, never the person's whole reachability.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it. The message names no campaign: it goes outside any of the provider's.

follows.description: Which earlier letter the message follows, composed by the runtime at the claim from `args.follows` and the campaign's own earlier sends: never written by a caller. It says the whole decision: a letter followed, by its work item, its operation and the provider's reference for that send, or, with all three null, a new letter; `because` says why either way. A plugin places the message by this member and by nothing in `args`.

work_item.description: The work item that sent the letter followed, or null for a new letter.

operation.description: The operation that sent it, `message.send`, or null for a new letter.

reference.description: The provider's reference for the send followed, as that work item's succeeded attempt returned it under `external_ids.send`, or null for a new letter.

because.description: Why: `named`, the caller named the letter followed in `args.follows`; `line_root`, the runtime followed the line's root; `asked_new_thread`, the caller asked for a letter of its own; `no_earlier_letter`, the line holds no earlier letter that can be followed; `not_offered`, the routed plugin does not take `follows` on this channel; `other_account`, the line's root went through another plugin or binding than this message is routed to; `other_mailbox`, the line's root went from another of the provider's accounts than `args.sender`.
